content.comment_body: Hello, I'm from Brazil. Can you help me? I'm having trouble connecting a [product_name] with article number [article_no]. I couldn't find it in [product_name] software [version_no], since it seems to connect only with [version_no].

It doesn't matter if you use [product_name] Soft Comfort [version_no] or [version_no]; either version should allow you to connect to the [product_name] [version_no]. What is the IP address and subnet mask of your PC or laptop? Is your [product_name] device connected directly to your PC/laptop or via a router? Did you change the IP address of your [product_name] device, or is it still set to the default?

I'm using a direct cable from the [product_name] to my laptop. I've changed the IP addresses on both the [product_name] device and the laptop's network adapter. I can ping the device successfully without any packet loss, but the firmware with article number [article_no] isn't listed in the software. Do you know how I can resolve this?
Communication works—when I test the connection with the [product_name] device and via the command prompt, I get a response.
Are the [product_name] device and your PC on the same subnet?

Yes, the [product_name] device has IP 192.168.0.100 and my laptop is at 192.168.0.101, both with subnet mask 255.255.255.0. However, my [product_name]'s firmware version (article number [article_no]) doesn't appear in the software list, which is the problem.
I suggest starting a support request for this issue.

Which operating system are you using? [product_name] Soft Comfort [version_no] is compatible with: Windows 7, 8, or 10; SUSE Linux 12 sp1, kernel 3.12.74, and other Linux distributions that support Java 2; and Mac OS X versions from 10.7 Lion up to 10.14 Mojave. Please make sure you have all required access rights on your OS. Additional tips: Since both devices are on the same subnet, leave the Default Gateway parameter empty. Direct Ethernet cable or an Ethernet switch can be used. A router would place the devices in different subnets, which doesn't fit your setup. It's also possible there is an Ethernet driver issue. The [product_name] device requires a standard TCP/IP driver.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing problems connecting to a [product_name] device using [product_name] Soft Comfort, especially in recognizing the hardware version within the software. Although network connectivity is confirmed via direct cable and correct subnet configuration, the main challenge is that the specific device (with article number [article_no]) isn't shown in the software interface. There is uncertainty about compatibility between the software and the hardware version.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable detection and connection of their [product_name] hardware in [product_name] Soft Comfort, regardless of the exact version involved. They want clear indication of supported hardware and firmware, along with straightforward setup and troubleshooting.
